title: Bioprinting of heterogeneous and multilayered cell-hydrogel constructs using continuous multi-material printing and aerosol-based crosslinking
protocol: Install the multibarrel nozzle and crosslinking aerosol tube on the printing head.
Assemble the stopper into the groove on the back of the printing head.
Mount the printing head onto the gantry.
Attach the prepared holders for the multibarrel nozzle holder and aerosol tube to the printing head.
Connect the Tygon tubes from the pneumatic pump to the metal tubes of the nozzle adapter.
Insert the fully assembled nozzle into the holder of the printing head.
Connect the PVC tube with a nebulizer.
Insert the aerosol tube into the holder of the printing head.
Mix food dye with pure alginate to prepare seven different colored 4% alginate inks.
Connect the prepared inks to the pumping system via Tygon reservoir and tube.
Prepare a 2% CaCl2 solution for gelation of the alginate construct after printing.
Prepare a 10% CaCl2 solution for fast gelation during printing using a nebulizer.
Fill the bioinks into the multibarrel nozzle by applying a pneumatic pressure of 2,000 mbar.
Check the extruded bioinks through the nozzle tip to ensure proper flow.
Turn off the pump to stop extrusion once the nozzle is confirmed functional.
Prepare the GCode for continuous printing and the pressure control program.
Turn on the nebulizer to supply a 10% CaCl2 aerosol before starting the print process.
Start the pumping program and the GCode simultaneously to begin continuous extrusion.
Immediately dip the printed sample into the crosslinking solution for 3 minutes after printing ends.
Wash the printed sample with Dulbecco’s phosphate-buffered saline (DPBS) three times.
Observe the sample on the microscope to optimize the printing conditions.
Apply pressure within the range from 200 mbar to 800 mbar for printing seven-different colored alginate inks.
Use a speed of 100 mm/min for printing seven-different colored alginate inks.
Print the complex biological construct such as the heterogeneous and multilayered cell-hydrogel construct under crosslinking aerosol.
Bring the four bioinks (cancer bioink, vascular bioink, fibroblast bioink, and supporting bioink).
Connect the bioinks to the pumping system via the Tygon reservoir and tube.
Fill the bioinks into the multibarrel nozzle by applying a pneumatic pressure of 2,000 mbar.
Apply a speed of 100 mm/min for filling the bioinks into the multibarrel nozzle.
Turn off the pump to stop extruding bioinks.
Turn on the nebulizer to supply a 10% CaCl2 aerosol.
Start the pumping program and print the GCode for the TME construct simultaneously.
Harvest the printed sample immediately after printing ends.
Dip the harvested sample into the crosslinking solution for 3 minutes.
Wash the printed TME construct with DPBS three times.
Dip the TME construct into the EGM-2 culture medium.

Check the heterogeneous multilayered TME construct by observing green fluorescent cancer cells in the bottom layer and red fluorescent vascular endothelial cells in the top layer on a microscope or confocal microscope.
Fix the TME construct for immunostaining.
Dilute CD-31 antibody to 1/100 in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Treat fixed TME construct with diluted CD-31 antibody.
Incubate treated TME construct at 4°C for 24 hours.
Analyze morphological characteristics of cancer cells and vascular endothelial cells tri-cultured in the printed TME.
